name: How to Create a json-schema Atom
summary: Step-by-step tutorial for publishing a JSON Schema document as a json-schema type atom in schema-atoms.

tutorial_profile.outcome: You have a valid json-schema atom file committed to schema-atoms/atoms/ and can reference it by its stable atom ID from any catalog.

body.inline:
## Overview

A *json-schema atom* is a versioned JSON Schema document stored in schema-atoms and addressable by a stable ID. Once published, any catalog can reference it in its grammar atom or validator configuration.

## Steps

### 1. Identify the schema you want to publish

Decide the logical name for your schema. Use kebab-case. Examples: `persona-v1`, `prompt-fragment-v1`, `key-rotation-policy-v1`. The name becomes the atom ID and must be unique across schema-atoms.

### 2. Create the schema file

```bash
# Inside a feat/* worktree on schema-atoms
mkdir -p atoms/json-schema
touch atoms/json-schema/<your-name>.json
```

Start with the canonical header:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://schema-atoms.com/schemas/<your-name>.json",
  "title": "<Human readable title>",
  "description": "<One sentence: what this schema validates>",
  "type": "object",
  "required": [],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {}
}
```

### 3. Write the atom wrapper

Every schema-atoms atom has a JSON wrapper that conforms to the schema-atoms atom-v1 grammar. Create `atoms/json-schema/<your-name>-atom.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "https://schema-atoms.com/schemas/atom-v1.json",
  "type": "json-schema",
  "id": "<your-name>",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "name": "<Human-readable name>",
  "summary": "<One sentence summary>",
  "audience": ["contributor"],
  "tags": [],
  "body": {
    "format": "markdown",
    "inline": "Inline description or leave path to the .json schema file."
  }
}
```

### 4. Run the validator

```bash
cd schema-atoms
python3 scripts/validate.py
```

Fix any validation errors reported against `atom-v1.json` before continuing.

### 5. Sign the atom

```bash
node scripts/sign-atoms.mjs
```

This requires the 1Password CLI (`op`) authenticated to the "Convergent Systems LLC" vault. The script writes signatures to `keys/`.

### 6. Commit and open a PR

```bash
git add atoms/json-schema/<your-name>.json atoms/json-schema/<your-name>-atom.json keys/
git commit -m "feat: add <your-name> json-schema atom v0.1.0"
git push origin feat/<your-name>
gh pr create --repo convergent-systems-co/schema-atoms
```

The CI workflow validates all atoms on every PR. Merge only after CI is green.

## Verification

After merging, confirm the atom is resolvable:

```bash
curl https://schema-atoms.com/atoms/json-schema/<your-name>.json
```

You should receive the atom JSON with a 200 status code.
